name: Alberta Innovates HYRS: University of Alberta
stipend: ~$15/hr (30–35 hrs/week)
eligibility: Grade 11, north of Red Deer, 85%+ in Math 20, Bio 20, and one other science
description: Applications close in mid-March for the July–August placement. Paid six-week summer health research at the U of A with a ~$3,000 stipend, cohort programming and a closing poster symposium.

name: Alberta Innovates HYRS: University of Calgary
stipend: $3,000 stipend
eligibility: Grade 11, south of Red Deer to north of Claresholm, 85%+ in Math 20, Bio 20, and one other science
description: Applications close in mid-March for the July–August placement. Paid summer research in biomedical and health sciences at UCalgary, with cohort programming, guest lectures and a poster symposium.

name: Alberta Innovates HYRS: University of Lethbridge
stipend: $3,000 stipend
eligibility: Grade 11, in or south of Claresholm, 85%+ in Math 20, Bio 20, and one other science
description: Applications close in late March for the July–August placement. Paid six-week health research placement at ULethbridge with cohort programming and a closing poster symposium.

name: WISEST Summer Research Program
stipend: Paid research assistantship
eligibility: Grade 11 students; focus on underrepresented groups in STEM, open to all genders
description: Student applications open in early March and close in early April for the July-August placement. Paid summer research at the U of A for students underrepresented in STEM, ending with a celebration event in August.

name: FEM+ Engineering Mentorship Program
provider: Faculty of Engineering, University of Alberta
eligibility: Women high school students interested in engineering
description: A seven-month mentorship for female, non-binary and 2SLGBTQ+ high school students, with info sessions, faculty events, campus tours and design challenges in the Elko Engineering Garage. The 2025/26 cohort is closed; watch DiscoverE for the next intake.

name: ELITE Program for Black Youth
stipend: Paid internship
eligibility: Black youth aged 15–22 interested in STEM
description: Applications are accepted through the DiscoverE form, with separate intern streams in Edmonton and Ottawa. ELITE is a paid summer program for Black youth in innovation, technology and entrepreneurship.

name: TeamUP Science
eligibility: Inner-city, rural, and Indigenous students
description: Alberta-based mentorship and experiential learning for students underrepresented in STEM.

name: SHAD Canada
stipend: Financial aid available
eligibility: Grades 10–11, strong academics, leadership
description: Applications for SHAD 2027 open in mid-September and close in early January. Month-long STEAM program on a Canadian university campus: solve real-world problems in teams, live in residence, and build a cross-country network.

name: Sanofi Biogenius Canada Competition
eligibility: Alberta high school students grades 9-12 interested in life sciences research
description: Heads up: the Biogenius Canada site is offline — biogenius.ca now redirects to Sanofi’s corporate page. Students are paired with scientist mentors for an original life-sciences research project presented at regional and national competitions.

name: Youreka Canada
eligibility: Alberta high school students grades 9-12 interested in citizen science research
description: A 10-week research and mentorship program where students create and contribute to a citizen science project guided by an undergraduate student mentor. Students develop research skills, collect real data, and present findings.

name: RBC Summer Tech Labs
stipend: Paid (hourly rate in offer letter)
eligibility: Grades 11-12 at an Ontario-based high school (no longer open to Alberta students)
description: Applications for summer 2027 reopen in spring 2027. An 8-week paid internship building working prototypes for real RBC business problems in JavaScript and React, with tech talks and mentorship.

name: VJKF Indigenous Science and Engineering Program
provider: Verna J. Kirkness Foundation (multiple Canadian universities)
eligibility: Indigenous (First Nation, Métis, and Inuit) high school students in grades 10-12
description: Applications for the 2027 program reopen in fall 2026. A one-week program where Indigenous high school students conduct research alongside university professors and graduate students at the U of A.

name: Canada-Wide Science Fair (CWSF)
location: National (2026 CWSF hosted in Edmonton, AB)
eligibility: Canadian students in grades 7–12; must first qualify through a regional science fair (e.g., Southeastern Alberta RSF, CYSF)
description: CWSF 2027 runs May 29 – June 5 in Hamilton. There is no direct application: Alberta students qualify by winning at their regional science fair, then present original research against roughly 400 finalists from across Canada.

name: iGEM High School Competition
eligibility: High school students worldwide; requires a school or community lab sponsor and a teacher or faculty PI
description: Team registration for the 2026 season is closed. iGEM's High School Competition is entered as a school team under a teacher acting as PI, not by individual students; teams design a synthetic biology project across the season for the international jamboree.

name: STEM Fellowship Big Data & AI Challenge
location: National/virtual + in-person finale in Calgary, AB
eligibility: Canadian high school students grades 9–12; teams of up to 5; no coding experience required
description: This challenge is not currently running — STEM Fellowship lists no active Big Data & AI Challenge cycle. Teams previously produced a peer-reviewed manuscript from open-data and AI research, with a finale in Calgary.

name: MindFuel geekStarter
eligibility: Alberta students in grades 7–12; teams form through school or community; all STEM fields welcome including robotics, biotech, ICT
description: Alberta-exclusive project-based STEM innovation program where student teams tackle real-world problems using emerging technologies. Teams receive mentorship and may advance to MindFuel's national Tech Futures Challenge.

name: MindFuel Tech Futures Challenge
location: National (AB, BC, SK, MB, ON, QC, NB), in-person events in Alberta
eligibility: Students in grades 7–12 from participating provinces; self-organized teams
description: National innovation challenge where youth teams design and prototype STEM solutions to real-world problems. Teams receive access to industry mentors, workshops, and MindFuel's Connect2Innovate platform. 13+ years running with 5,000+ alumni.

name: Tate High School Internship Program (HIP)
provider: Department of Computing Science, University of Alberta
stipend: Paid internship
eligibility: High school students (Grade 11–12) with strong interest in computing; open to all genders
description: Status unclear: the U of A's HIP page states the program "will no longer be offered for Summer 2025 and onwards", while the department's Explore page still says Tate internship applications open in the spring. Confirm with Computing Science before counting on it.

name: STEM Fellowship Research Exploration Program – Edmonton
eligibility: High school students grades 9–12
description: Applications are open now across host universities including UCalgary, UBC, Queens, Guelph, York, TMU and U of T Mississauga. REO places high school students on real research, prioritising Indigenous, rural, refugee, newcomer and first-generation students — though everyone is encouraged to apply.

name: Future Creators – University of Alberta
provider: Faculty of Engineering, University of Alberta
eligibility: High school students interested in engineering; open to all
description: Free program connecting high school students with UAlberta engineering students for virtual mentorship. Project materials are shipped to participants' homes for hands-on engineering projects guided remotely.

name: Cybermentors – University of Calgary
provider: Schulich School of Engineering, University of Calgary
eligibility: High school girls/young women interested in science and engineering
description: The mentorship program is currently on hiatus at UCalgary. It connected high school girls with women in science and engineering through mentorship, networking and industry exposure.

name: Destination Exploration – University of Lethbridge
eligibility: High school students; southern Alberta focus
description: The high-school stream is InSRA, a six-week paid Indigenous Summer Research Academy ($3,000 award, plus a $500 travel bursary) for students who have completed Grade 11, running alongside HYRS at ULethbridge. There is also a 3-week paid summer intern role for Gr 9+. Dates for the next cycle are not yet posted.

name: DiscoverE High School Initiatives – University of Alberta
provider: Faculty of Engineering, University of Alberta
eligibility: High school students interested in engineering and applied science
description: Suite of specialized summer engineering and science workshops at UAlberta featuring project-based research, prototyping, and hands-on lab experience. Includes multiple programs for various interests and demographics.

name: Alberta Junior Forest Rangers (JFR)
provider: Government of Alberta – Forestry and Parks
stipend: Government of Alberta wages
eligibility: Ages 16–18, Canadian citizen or permanent resident, physically fit
description: A paid summer job, not a course — full-time high school students aged 16 to 18 join a crew learning forestry, wildfire and conservation work across Alberta. Watch alis.alberta.ca for the intake, which opens over the winter.

name: WILD Outside – Canadian Wildlife Federation
eligibility: Youth aged 13–18 with an interest in conservation and the outdoors
description: Free conservation research and leadership program connecting youth 15–18 with nature through hands-on environmental research and conservation projects. Active programming available in Edmonton and Calgary areas.

name: Let's Talk Science – Space Lab / Tomatosphere
provider: Let's Talk Science / Canadian Space Agency
duration: Varies by initiative (ongoing through school year)
eligibility: Alberta high school students, accessed through their school
description: National citizen science initiatives accessible through Alberta high schools. Space Lab and Tomatosphere allow students to collect and analyze real environmental and spatial data, contributing to actual ongoing scientific research.

name: International Summer School for Young Physicists (ISSYP)
stipend: Fully funded (travel, accommodation, meals)
eligibility: Grade 11–12 Canadian and international students; highly competitive selection
description: Highly competitive 2-week fully funded summer school at Perimeter Institute for exceptional Grade 11/12 physics students. Features lectures by world-leading theoretical physicists and hands-on research exposure.

name: Quantum School for Young Students (QSYS)
provider: Institute for Quantum Computing, University of Waterloo
stipend: Subsidized (accommodation and meals included)
eligibility: Grade 11–12 Canadian students with strong math and physics background
description: Applications typically close in mid-May for the August session. Week-long dive into quantum information science and cryptography at IQC, University of Waterloo (formerly QCSYS), with lectures, labs and direct researcher access.

name: Blueprint – University of Toronto
provider: University of Toronto Faculty of Applied Science & Engineering
eligibility: Black high school students in grades 10–11 interested in engineering and applied research
description: Applications open in late November and close in mid-April for the following summer. A free U of T engineering program: a July intensive on the St. George campus, followed by biweekly events from October through February.

name: Medicine Youth Summer Program (Med YSP) – UofT
provider: University of Toronto, Faculty of Medicine
eligibility: Grades 10–12 (Grade 9 eligible for the microbiology module); open to students across Canada. Tuition applies (~$1,700 per module)
description: Postponed — U of T states Med YSP is pushed to Summer 2027. The program runs hands-on medical modules (human physiology, microbiology) with labs, lectures and discussions for high school students, open to Canadian and international applicants.

name: Calgary/Edmonton Brain Bee
eligibility: Alberta high school students
description: Regional neuroscience knowledge competitions for high school students in Calgary and Edmonton. Winners advance to the national Brain Bee where competitors analyze brain tissue and patient diagnoses. Top finishers represent Canada internationally.

name: Immerse Education Virtual Summer School – Research Track
eligibility: High school students worldwide; tuition fee applies
description: Online academic program where students work directly with university tutors to research and draft a university-level paper. Research tracks available in medicine, computer science, engineering, and more. Builds academic writing and independent research skills.

name: CAP High School Prize Exam
eligibility: Alberta high school students with interest in physics
description: Annual national physics exam where top regional performers earn recognition and networking opportunities with university physics labs. Preparation involves deep independent physics research. Top Alberta students often receive connections to university physics programs.

name: Technovation Girls – Alberta
eligibility: Young women and girls aged 13–18
description: Global tech education program where teams of young women identify a community problem, conduct user research, and build a mobile app or AI solution. Alberta participants can work remotely or through local hubs. Teams pitch to a panel of tech industry judges.

name: HOSA Canada – Future Health Professionals
eligibility: Alberta high school students interested in health sciences; students can start a chapter at their own school
description: International organization supporting health science students (no separate Canadian entity). Students conduct deep research to compete in events spanning biomedical laboratory science, epidemiology, and medical law. Canadian students can form local chapters at their own high schools and compete at HOSA international levels.

name: FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) – Canadian Rockies Region
location: Alberta (Calgary and Edmonton teams; regional events in AB)
eligibility: High school students grades 9–12; join or start a team
description: Rigorous engineering challenge where high school teams design, program, and build industrial-size robots in a 6-week build season. Requires applied research in mechanics, CAD, and control systems. Many Alberta teams compete in the Canadian Rockies regional event.

name: CERN Beamline for Schools (BL4S)
duration: Several months (proposal) + fully-funded experiment trip for winners
stipend: Fully funded trip to particle accelerator for winning teams
eligibility: High school students worldwide; teams of 2–9
description: Applications close in mid-March each year — the 2026 round closed 13 March. Teams of high school students propose an experiment to run on a real particle-accelerator beamline at CERN, and winning teams travel to carry it out.

name: Conrad Challenge
eligibility: High school students ages 13–18; teams of 2–5
description: Phase 1 (Activation) of the 2026-27 Conrad Challenge runs August 27 to October 30, 2026; Phase 2 (Innovation) closes January 8, 2027, with the Innovation Summit April 21-24, 2027. Student teams pitch a commercially viable solution to a real-world problem.

name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
stipend: Grand prize: $250,000 scholarship + lab for school
eligibility: Students aged 13–18 worldwide
description: Global science and math research competition. Students research a complex concept in life sciences, physics, or mathematics and translate that research into an engaging explanatory video (max 3 min). Grand prize includes a $250,000 scholarship.

name: Students on Ice (SOI) Foundation Expeditions
stipend: Competitive scholarships available (fully funded)
eligibility: High school students; highly competitive scholarship selection
description: Fully funded scholarships for high school students to join scientific expeditions to the Arctic or Antarctic. Students conduct hands-on environmental and climate field research alongside polar scientists, Indigenous knowledge holders, and global youth peers.

name: PIMS High School Programs – UAlberta / UCalgary
provider: Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences (PIMS)
eligibility: High school students with strong interest in mathematics
description: Specialized summer math camps, research workshops, and advanced problem-solving seminars hosted in partnership with UAlberta and UCalgary. Exposes students to university-level mathematical research and connects them with professional mathematicians.

name: APEGA Science Olympics
provider: APEGA (Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta)
eligibility: Alberta high school students; teams of 4–6
description: The 2025–26 season has concluded; next year's events are posted in the fall. Province-wide engineering and geoscience competition where high school teams solve timed, hands-on STEM challenges. Regionals feed the provincial finals.

name: Inside Education Youth Summits
stipend: Fully funded (travel, accommodation, meals)
eligibility: Alberta high school students; nominated or applied through school
description: Fully-funded regional summits covering themes like Energy, Water, and Agriculture. High school teams attend expert workshops, conduct environmental field research, and develop action plans to implement back in their local communities.

name: CyberTitan – National Cybersecurity Competition
location: Virtual + in-person nationals (open to Alberta teams)
eligibility: Canadian high school students grades 9–12; teams of up to 15
description: Your teacher registers the team between April and October; the season runs October to May with a national finale. Teams defend simulated networks in real-time cyber defence scenarios — registration is open to educators, not to students directly.

name: Canadian Computing Competition (CCC)
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing
eligibility: High school students at participating Alberta schools
description: Premier Canadian programming and algorithm design challenge hosted by the University of Waterloo. Students apply advanced computer science and algorithmic research to solve complex problems. Top scorers are invited to the Canadian Computing Olympiad (CCO).

name: Canadian Biology Olympiad (CBO)
eligibility: Canadian high school students; grades 11–12 recommended
description: The national exam is written in early April, with a training camp at UBC Okanagan for those selected. The Canadian Biology Olympiad is the qualifying route toward Canada's International Biology Olympiad team.

name: Team Canada – Regeneron ISEF
provider: Youth Science Canada / Society for Science
stipend: Travel funded for selected Team Canada members
eligibility: Alberta students who qualify through a regional science fair (e.g., CYSF, SARSF); top projects advance to CWSF, then ISEF selection
description: No direct application — Canadian students qualify for Regeneron ISEF through a Society-affiliated regional science fair. The world’s largest pre-college science competition; Team Canada selection is highly competitive.

name: The Junior Academy – New York Academy of Sciences
location: Virtual (fully online, open to Alberta students)
eligibility: High school students aged 13–17 worldwide; competitive application
description: Applications open April 1 and close in early July, with decisions by August 31. A free online research program from the New York Academy of Sciences where students team up on industry-set challenges with a mentor.

name: Pioneer Academics Research Program
location: Virtual (online, open to Alberta students); need-based aid available
eligibility: High school students grades 10–12; competitive application; financial aid available
description: Rigorous virtual research institute for high school students. Accepted students work one-on-one with university professors across disciplines, from neuroscience to computer science, to produce a peer-reviewed research paper over 8 weeks.

name: CMHF Discovery Days in Health Sciences
location: University of Alberta (Edmonton) and University of Calgary
eligibility: High school students; apply through CMHF or school
description: Student registration opens roughly six weeks before each event and is handled through your school's contact teacher. Discovery Days bring students onto a medical campus for hands-on health-science workshops and career panels with clinicians and researchers.

name: Caring for our Watersheds – Alberta
stipend: Winners receive funding to implement their project
eligibility: Alberta high school students grades 9–12
description: Environmental research and proposal competition. Students research a local watershed issue, write a detailed solution proposal, and compete for funding to implement their project in their community. Top Alberta entries advance to regional and national judging.

name: 4-H Alberta Senior Projects
eligibility: Alberta high school students enrolled in 4-H; open to non-farm youth
description: Senior-level 4-H streams involve rigorous, independent, multi-month research projects in veterinary science, agribusiness, and environmental stewardship. Projects culminate in regional and provincial presentations judged by industry professionals.

name: Amii K-12 AI Literacy
eligibility: Reached through your school. Amii supplies the kits and sessions to teachers, so ask a science or CTS teacher to request one
description: Free curriculum-aligned AI learning kits and guest speaker sessions that Amii provides to Alberta schools, including an AI in Junior High stream. Delivered by your teachers rather than applied to directly, so the way in is asking a teacher to bring it into your classroom.

name: Canada Learning Code – Teen Programs
eligibility: Teens aged 13–17; no prior coding experience required
description: Discontinued. Canada Learning Code wound down its teen programming (the Teen Ambassador Program closed in July 2024) and its current workshops are restricted to adults 18+.

name: Dual Credit – Medicine Hat Public School Division
provider: MHPSD with Medicine Hat College, Olds College, SAIT and Lethbridge Polytechnic
eligibility: Grade 10–12 students at MHPSD schools; apply through your school
description: Enrol through your school counsellor rather than applying separately. Dual Credit lets Medicine Hat Public students take real post-secondary courses while in high school, earning 5 to 30-level high school credits plus 3 post-secondary credits per course.

name: Polygence Research Program
location: Virtual (online, open to Alberta students); tuition fee applies, need-based aid available
eligibility: High school students grades 9–12 worldwide; competitive application; financial aid available
description: Virtual research academy matching high school students with PhD mentors for a 10-week independent research project in any discipline. Projects result in a finalized research paper, podcast, or technical prototype. Strong portfolio-building program.

name: The Knowledge Society (TKS)
eligibility: High school students grades 9–12; competitive application
description: Applications for the 2026-27 cohort are open now. TKS is a 10-month after-school program where students go deep on AI, biotech and robotics and build projects with companies; alumni have reached research labs and startups before 19.

name: Qubit by Qubit – High School Quantum Computing
location: Virtual (online, open to Alberta students); need-based aid available
eligibility: High school students worldwide; no prior quantum or coding experience required
description: Summer research applications are open now, and the signature Introduction to Quantum Computing course runs from October. Qubit by Qubit teaches quantum computing to high school students, taught by PhD researchers with Google Quantum AI.

name: Student Spaceflight Experiments Program (SSEP)
provider: National Center for Earth and Space Science Education (NCESSE)
location: School-based (must be in a participating school district)
eligibility: High school students at participating schools; teams of 3–6
description: Open only where your school or district has joined SSEP as a community — those teams design flight experiments from September 1 to November 3, 2026, with community submissions to NCESSE by November 12 for Mission 22 to the International Space Station.

name: Canadian Chemistry Olympiad (CCO)
duration: Self-study + Canadian Chemistry Contest (April) + national camp for finalists
location: Province-wide (school-based); national training camp for finalists
eligibility: Canadian high school students; grades 11–12 recommended
description: Highest level of chemistry competition for Canadian youth. You enter through the Canadian Chemistry Contest in April, which the Chemical Institute of Canada runs and uses to select for the Olympiad; national-team candidates then work through online problem sets, a take-home exam and a national camp. Preparation goes far beyond the high school curriculum, into organic, inorganic and physical chemistry. Top students represent Canada at the International Chemistry Olympiad.

name: Sir Isaac Newton (SIN) Physics Exam
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing
eligibility: High school students at participating Alberta schools
description: Registration opens in mid-March; the exam is written at your school on the first Thursday of May. A demanding open-ended physics exam from the University of Waterloo that rewards months of independent study.

name: GreenLearning Innovation Challenges
eligibility: Alberta high school students and eco-clubs; accessed through school or independently
description: Challenges like Decoding Carbon and Energy Revealed prompt students to research local energy consumption or climate policy, then design and implement a data-backed emissions reduction strategy for their school or municipality.

name: Agriculture in the Classroom Canada (AITC)
eligibility: Alberta high school students interested in agriculture and food systems
description: Students research global food security, agricultural technology, and sustainability, then pitch solutions to real agricultural problems with input from industry mentors.

name: Historica Canada – Heritage Fairs & Young Citizens
eligibility: Canadian students grades 7–12; accessed through school or independently
description: Heritage Fairs and Young Citizens are no longer listed by Historica Canada — they appear on neither the current nor the past programs page, and /heritagefairs returns a 404. Historica now runs the Citizenship Challenge, Heritage Minutes and The Memory Project.

name: VEX Robotics Competition – Alberta Leagues
provider: Robotics Education & Competition Foundation / VEX Robotics
duration: Season-long (fall–spring) with local, regional, and provincial tournaments
eligibility: High school students; join or start a school or community team
description: Applied engineering challenge where student teams research, design, build, and program autonomous and driver-controlled robots to compete in game-based tournaments. Highly accessible with events hosted locally across Alberta's regional school districts.

name: FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC) – Alberta
duration: Season-long (fall–spring) with regional and provincial events
eligibility: Students grades 7–12; join or start a school or community team
description: Distinct from the larger FRC, FTC teams design, build, and program smaller-scale robots using Java and Android-based technology. Requires applied research into control systems and computer vision. More accessible entry point than FRC with lower build costs.

name: STEM Racing Canada (F1 in Schools)
provider: F1 in Schools / STEM Racing Canada
eligibility: High school students grades 9–12; teams of 3–6
description: Multidisciplinary engineering competition where teams use CAD and CAM software to research aerodynamics, design, and race miniature compressed-air powered F1 cars. Alberta teams actively compete at national championships. Builds skills in design, manufacturing, and project management.

name: Hack the North – High School Track
stipend: Travel grants available for accepted out-of-province students
location: Waterloo, Ontario (in-person); open to Alberta applicants
eligibility: High school students (and undergraduate); competitive application
description: Hacker applications for the September 18-20, 2026 event are closed; the next cycle opens the following summer. Canada's largest hackathon brings 1,000+ students to Waterloo for 36 hours of building, with travel, food and lodging covered.

name: CyberSci – Cyber Security Challenge Canada (High School)
duration: Several months (regional CTF events + national finals)
location: Virtual (CTF events) + in-person nationals (open to Alberta teams)
eligibility: Canadian high school students; teams or individuals
description: Ethical hacking competition where teams research network vulnerabilities, cryptography, and server security, then compete in simulated real-time Capture the Flag (CTF) events. Regional and national levels with Alberta participation.

name: DEEP Summer Academy – University of Toronto
location: Toronto, Ontario (in-person); open to Alberta students; tuition fee applies
eligibility: High school students grades 10–12; strong academic record; bursaries available
description: Applications open in early March in two rounds — an early-bird round at a lower fee, then a second round through mid-April. DEEP is a paid U of T engineering summer academy running July to mid-August on the St. George campus.

name: LaunchX Virtual Summer Program
location: Virtual (online, open to Alberta students); tuition fee applies, need-based aid available
eligibility: High school students grades 9–12; competitive application; financial aid available
description: Rigorous global entrepreneurship program where high schoolers form teams to conduct deep market research, prototype a digital or physical tech product, and pitch a fully functioning startup to a panel of investors. MIT-affiliated curriculum.

name: TELUS Spark Science Centre Volunteering – Calgary
eligibility: Age 16 and older; 14 and older for summer camp volunteering
description: Volunteer alongside science communicators at Calgary's science centre, running workshops, staffing exhibits and supporting summer camps. A steady way into science outreach experience, and one of the few STEM volunteer roles in Calgary open at 14 through the camp stream.

name: Alberta Computers for Schools – CFS+ Internship
stipend: Paid internship
eligibility: Older high school students and recent graduates in Alberta
description: Provides paid IT, hardware, and network configuration work experience for older high school students and recent graduates. Students refurbish and deploy computer equipment while building real-world technical skills.

name: Cisco Networking Academy – High School Stream
eligibility: High school students at participating Alberta schools
description: Delivered through Alberta school boards, allowing students to research network vulnerabilities and earn industry-recognized certifications in cybersecurity, networking, and IT fundamentals directly through their high school.

name: IBM SkillsBuild for High School
eligibility: High school students with an interest in AI, web development, or cloud computing
description: Virtual platform with active Canadian school partnerships providing mentorship and micro-credentials in artificial intelligence, web development, and cloud computing. Students earn IBM-recognized badges upon completion.

name: Apple Swift Student Challenge
eligibility: Students enrolled in an educational institution; age 18 or under for student category
description: Premier global coding competition where high school app developers design, research, and submit an original Swift playground or iOS app. Winners receive exclusive Apple development tools, WWDC access, and global recognition.

name: Microsoft Imagine Cup Junior
eligibility: Students aged 13–18 worldwide
description: Discontinued. Microsoft no longer runs the junior track, and the remaining Imagine Cup is restricted to enrolled students aged 18 and over, so it is not a high school option.

name: Hackergal
location: Virtual + in-person events in Alberta (Calgary, Edmonton)
eligibility: Young women in grades 6–12
description: National hackathons and virtual coding clubs where young women build their first web and software projects. No coding experience required.

name: UAlberta Game + AI Bootcamps
provider: Department of Computing Science, University of Alberta
eligibility: High school students interested in game development and AI
description: Specialized enrichment bootcamps run by UAlberta's Computing Science department focusing on applying machine learning algorithms to game design and logic. Students explore AI concepts through hands-on programming projects.

name: Medicine Hat College Summer STEM & Tech Camps
eligibility: High school students in Southeast Alberta
description: These are childrens camps — Rattlers Athletics and the Child Development Centre run them for ages 6-17, with much of the programming aimed at elementary ages rather than senior high school research.

name: Southeast Alberta Regional Science Fair (SEARSF)
provider: Youth Science Canada / Medicine Hat College
eligibility: Students in Southeast Alberta grades 7–12
description: Registration opens in the fall, with regional fairs held between February and April. Winning at this regional fair is the only route to the Canada-Wide Science Fair for students in southeastern Alberta.

name: UCalgary Active Living Summer Camps
provider: Active Living, Faculty of Kinesiology, University of Calgary
eligibility: Camp options run from entering grade 4 up to entering grade 11; registration fee applies
description: Registration is closed — UCalgary states the camp form "is no longer available" while the service is being updated. Active Living runs multi-sport and recreation summer camps on campus; sign up for their notification list for the next intake.

name: Canadian Sport Institute Calgary – Youth Seminars
eligibility: High school students interested in sports science and elite athletics
description: Exposure to Olympic-level sports science, biometric tracking, and physiological recovery research at state-of-the-art testing facilities used by Canada's national athletes. Students learn how elite performance data is collected and analyzed.

name: AHS Youth Volunteer & Research Programs
location: Alberta-wide including South Zone hospitals and clinics
eligibility: High school students 15+; application through local AHS facility
description: Volunteer placements in AHS regional hospitals and clinics offering direct exposure to clinical environments, health administration, and medical technology. South Zone placements available for students in Lethbridge, Medicine Hat, and surrounding communities.

name: Canadian Open Mathematics Challenge (COMC)
eligibility: Canadian high school students; administered through participating schools
description: Your teacher registers the school by October 22 (October 15 for shipped exams); the contest is written October 29, 2026. Independent registration opens around September 16 only if your school is not participating. Top scorers are invited to the Canadian Mathematical Olympiad.

name: Royal Astronomical Society of Canada – Youth Programs
eligibility: High school students interested in astronomy and astrophysics
description: Calgary and Edmonton RASC chapters offer high school students direct access to telescopes, observatories, and astrophysical research mentorship. Students participate in observation nights, star parties, and research workshops alongside amateur and professional astronomers.

name: TRIUMF High School Fellowship
stipend: Paid research fellowship
location: Vancouver, BC (in-person); open to Alberta applicants
eligibility: Grade 11–12 students across Canada; highly competitive; strong physics and math background
description: Open only to graduating secondary students in British Columbia entering first-year post-secondary — Alberta students are not eligible. Now called the YES Fellowship: a six-week paid summer research term at TRIUMF with an award of about $4,500 plus travel and housing.

name: Let's Talk Science – University Chapter Symposia
provider: Let's Talk Science / University chapters (UAlberta, UCalgary)
eligibility: Alberta high school students; registration through school or directly
description: High-level, day-long symposiums run by UAlberta and UCalgary LTS chapters on niche topics like stem cell research, space exploration, and AI ethics. Distinct from the Space Lab/Tomatosphere citizen science programs; these are lecture and lab-based days for high schoolers.

name: Ocean Networks Canada – Youth Advisory Council
provider: Ocean Networks Canada (ONC) / University of Victoria
eligibility: High school students interested in data science and environmental research
description: Open to Albertans interested in data science and the environment. Students analyze massive open-source data sets relating to marine biology, ocean chemistry, and climate from ONC's global sensor network. Virtual participation accessible from anywhere in Canada.

name: MacEwan University Design Summer Camp
eligibility: Students entering grades 9 to 12; registration fee applies
description: The camp runs the last week of July, with registration closing in mid-July. A five-day MacEwan design camp covering graphic design, app design, illustration, photography and videography.

name: Alberta University of the Arts – Pre-College Programs
eligibility: Ages 16–18 who have completed Grade 10, 11 or 12; tuition applies
description: For students aged 16+: Pre-College is a four-week summer immersive covering both Fine Art and Design at university level, and Arts-Bridge is a shorter two-week introduction for students who cannot commit to the full month.

name: Olds College High School Ag-Tech Programs
eligibility: Alberta high school students grades 10–12 with interest in ag-tech
description: Bootcamps and dual-credit courses focusing on the intersection of agriculture, drone telemetry, precision farming, and data science. Students use Olds College's smart farm and tech facilities.

name: Forum for Young Canadians
stipend: Subsidized; bursaries available
location: Ottawa, Ontario (in-person); open to Alberta students
eligibility: Canadian high school students grades 10–12; school nomination or independent application
description: Applications for Forum 2027 open soon, for sessions running February 7-12, February 28 - March 5, and April 18-23, 2027. Three hundred students aged 15-18 spend a week in Ottawa meeting MPs and Senators; travel, meals and accommodation are covered, with bursaries against the $995 fee.

name: YMCA Youth Exchanges Canada
stipend: Funded (travel and accommodation covered)
location: Various Canadian provinces (open to Alberta students)
eligibility: Youth aged 12–17 travelling as a group of 10–30 with a group leader, not as an individual applicant
description: A funded reciprocal exchange that twins a group of Alberta youth with a group from another province or territory, each hosting the other for at least five days. Groups plan their own travel, budget, itinerary and community project. Applications are made by a group leader, so you need a teacher or community organizer to run it.

name: CAREERS: The Next Generation – High School Internships
duration: 75–125 hours per semester (extendable to 500 hours); part-time in the school year or full-time in summer
stipend: Alberta minimum wage or higher
location: Alberta-wide (employer work sites across the province)
eligibility: Any student registered at an Alberta school, generally from grade 10; placement arranged with a participating employer
description: Paid internships that place high school students with Alberta employers in skilled trades, ICT, health, agriculture, forestry and energy. Students earn high school credits while working and can roll a placement into a Registered Apprenticeship. Free to students; start dates vary across the province.

name: Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP)
duration: 125 hours of on-the-job learning per 5-credit RAP course; up to 1,000 apprenticeship hours
stipend: At least Alberta minimum wage
eligibility: Senior high school students aged 15+ with parent or guardian consent; must complete HCS3000 Workplace Safety Systems and find an employer willing to supervise and train
description: Be a full-time student and a registered apprentice at the same time. Students split their week between school and an approved work site, earning one high school credit for every 25 hours on the job (up to 41 credits), while those hours also count toward journeyperson certification. Free application through Apprenticeship and Industry Training.

name: Skills Canada Alberta – Provincial Skills Competition
duration: Regional and qualifying rounds through the winter; two-day provincial competition in May
stipend: Medals and prizes; top competitors join Team Alberta for nationals
location: Alberta-wide (9 regional competitions; provincials in Edmonton)
eligibility: Alberta secondary students, entering through a Regional Skills Canada Competition, an online qualifier, or in-school selection where a skill is not offered regionally
description: Registration for the regional qualifiers opens in early January. Alberta students compete in trades and technology contests at regionals, with winners advancing to the provincial competition and on to Skills Canada nationals.

name: SAIT Dual Credit Programs
duration: Varies by program (typically one semester or a summer term)
stipend: No direct tuition cost to students or families
location: Calgary (SAIT campus) and partner high schools
eligibility: Alberta students in grades 11 and 12, enrolled through their high school
description: Earn high school credits and a post-secondary credential or workplace certification at the same time, across more than 20 options: skilled trades (welding, carpentry, pipe trades, automotive, heavy equipment), software and web development, IT, health care, aviation, business, culinary and construction. Offered at no direct tuition cost. Students enrol through their high school.

name: JA Southern Alberta – Company Program
stipend: Free of charge to students, teachers and schools
location: Calgary and southern Alberta (in-school or after-school)
eligibility: Students in grades 9–12 in southern Alberta; join through a class or register directly for an after-school cohort
description: JA Southern Alberta's flagship program: a student-led, mentor-supported team builds and runs a real company over 20 weeks, covering market research, financial planning, sales and a year-end tradeshow. Participants also get executive and sales training plus events like World of Choices. Runs in class or as an after-school activity at multiple Calgary locations.

name: JA Northern Alberta – Company Program
duration: Runs as an in-school or after-school cohort through the school year
location: Edmonton and northern Alberta (in-school, after-school, or self-directed)
eligibility: Northern Alberta students in grades 9–12; join through a school partnership or contact JA directly
description: Financial literacy, entrepreneurship and work readiness programming for northern Alberta students, including the after-school Company Program where a student team builds and runs a real business. Delivered in partnership with schools; self-directed options are also available.

name: Alberta Debate and Speech Association Tournaments
duration: Tournament season through the school year, with provincials in the spring
eligibility: Alberta students competing through a school-based speech and debate club; ADSA serves over 50 member schools
description: The provincial association for school-based speech and debate in Alberta, running junior and senior tournaments in English and French across Language Arts, Drama, Social Studies and Science. Builds research, argument construction and public speaking skills, and sends qualifiers to national and international competitions. Students take part through a club at their school.

name: Euclid Mathematics Contest
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing
location: School-based across Alberta (written at your own school); $18 per participant plus school order fees
eligibility: Senior secondary students; a contest supervisor at the school orders the contest and submits papers to the CEMC for marking
description: Canada's best-known senior high school mathematics contest, written each year by more than 25,000 students worldwide. Ten questions in 2.5 hours, mixing final-answer and full-solution problems. Results carry real weight in University of Waterloo admissions and scholarship decisions. Ask a math teacher to register the school. The ordering deadline is March 11, 2027 for the April 6, 2027 contest.

name: Pascal, Cayley and Fermat Mathematics Contests
provider: University of Waterloo – Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing
location: School-based across Alberta (written at your own school); $6 per participant plus school order fees
eligibility: Students in grades 9, 10 and 11 respectively; a contest supervisor at the school registers participants
description: The CEMC entry point to competitive mathematics before Euclid, with a separate contest for each of grades 9, 10 and 11. Twenty-five multiple-choice questions in 60 minutes, graded in three parts of increasing difficulty. A good first contest and the standard way Alberta students build toward Euclid and the Canadian Open Mathematics Challenge. Canadian schools order by February 9, 2027 for the February 23–24, 2027 contests.

name: Canadian Physics Olympiad (CPhO)
provider: Canadian Physics Olympiad – University of British Columbia
grades: High school (must be under 20 at the time of competition)
duration: Qualifying exam in April; national training camp at UBC in May
stipend: Travel funded for selected Team Canada members
location: Qualifying exam written at your school; national training camp at UBC, Vancouver
eligibility: Full-time student at a Canadian high school, Canadian citizen or permanent resident, not yet 20 at competition time, available for the full International Physics Olympiad period
description: The route to Team Canada at the International Physics Olympiad. Students qualify by writing the CAP High School Prize Exam (usually mid-April), and top scorers are invited to the national training camp at UBC in May, where the team is selected. High scorers who miss the May camp can join the online Canadian Junior Physics Olympiad camp in August. Talk to your physics teacher, since schools are notified each spring.

name: Canadian Geographic Challenge
provider: Canadian Geographic Education (Royal Canadian Geographical Society)
duration: Classroom and school rounds, then provincial and national finals
stipend: No cost to join
location: School-based across Alberta (online or print), with a national final
eligibility: Canadian students in grades 7–10 for Levels 1 and 2. Level 3 is open to ages 16–19 (before June 30) who are not yet in post-secondary, and needs only a supervisor, either a teacher or a guardian, to create the account.
description: National geography competition and Canada's route to the International Geography Olympiad. Levels 1 and 2 run through classroom and school rounds. Level 3 is the senior stream: a multimedia test open to everyone who signs up, narrowing to the top 20 for a written test, the top 10 for a fieldwork test, then six interviews and four Team Canada spots. Free to join, and a guardian can supervise if your school does not take part.

name: Bioengineering Summer Institute – University of Calgary
provider: Schulich School of Engineering, University of Calgary
duration: 4 weeks, weekdays 9 a.m.–4 p.m. (2026 session: July 27 – August 21)
stipend: $50 student fee; UCalgary covers the remaining ~$950 of the program cost
eligibility: Students who apply to UCalgary engineering with high school biology are automatically considered, with no separate application. Attendance is a condition of the admission offer.
description: Runs as a full-time summer course from late July to late August. The UCalgary Bioengineering Summer Institute gives high school students lab exposure to biomedical engineering ahead of a Schulich application.

name: High School Model UN – University of Calgary
provider: Department of Political Science, University of Calgary
eligibility: High school students from across Alberta, normally entering as a school delegation. Close to 30 schools and more than 500 delegates take part each year.
description: The longest standing Model UN conference for high school students in Alberta, run by the UCalgary political science department. Delegates represent countries across UN and NATO committees for two days, researching a national position, negotiating with blocs and drafting resolutions under formal debate rules. Good preparation for political science, law and international relations programs. The registration link goes live once the department announces the next conference date, so check the page in the fall.

name: Alberta Youth Parliament (TUXIS Parliament of Alberta)
provider: Alberta Youth Parliament / TUXIS Parliamentary Alumni Society of Alberta
duration: Winter session in the last week of December, plus regional events
eligibility: Any Alberta youth aged 15 to 21. No school nomination and no debate experience required. The parliament is non-denominational and open to members of any belief system.
description: The Alberta Youth Parliament website is currently down — abyp.ca shows only an "under construction" placeholder, with no session dates or application details posted. TUXIS Parliament has historically run a winter sitting for youth delegates.

name: Alberta High School Mathematics Competition (AHSMC)
provider: A.H.S.M.C. Board, hosted by the Department of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences, University of Alberta
grades: High school, plus junior high students recommended by a math teacher
duration: Two rounds: 80-minute Part I in November, 3-hour Part II in February
stipend: Fellowships awarded on Part II results
location: School-based across Alberta (written at your own school); $5 per extra Second Round nomination
eligibility: Alberta and Northwest Territories students. Part I is open to every eligible student; the top 50 scorers, plus the top five Grade 10 students, are invited to Part II. Schools register students with the A.H.S.M.C. Board.
description: Part I is written in November and Part II in early February; your school registers you. The Alberta High School Mathematics Competition is the province's longest-running math contest, run by the U of A.

name: NASA International Space Apps Challenge
provider: NASA, with local events hosted across Alberta
grades: Open to all ages; high school students compete on teams
location: Calgary and Edmonton local events, plus a global virtual option
eligibility: Open to anyone, with no cost to compete. Teams form at a local event or online and pick from the published challenge list.
description: The largest hackathon in the world, built entirely on open NASA and partner space agency data. Teams spend a weekend on a real challenge written by NASA experts, spanning software, data science, hardware, design and science storytelling. Alberta hubs ran in both Calgary and Edmonton in 2025. The 2026 edition runs November 14 to 15 with registration opening August 26, 2026, so check the site for the confirmed Alberta locations.

name: OAPT Grade 11 Physics Contest
provider: Ontario Association of Physics Teachers, sponsored by the University of Toronto Faculty of Applied Science and Engineering
grades: Students currently taking Grade 11 physics (Physics 20 in Alberta)
duration: 1 hour, 30 multiple-choice questions, written in May
location: School-based (written at your own school); free to enter
eligibility: Any student currently in Grade 11 physics. Students who have already started Grade 12 physics are not eligible. As of the 2026 contest the invitation is open to all schools, not only Ontario ones.
description: A one-hour, 30 question physics contest that opened to the rest of Canada in 2026, when OAPT extended its invitation beyond Ontario schools. Questions run from easy to difficult and reward physical intuition rather than formula memorization, which makes it a useful bridge between Physics 20 and the far harder CAP Prize Exam. Free to enter and non-programmable calculators are allowed. The 2026 contest ran May 20; a teacher can register the school up to a week before contest day.

name: The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award
provider: The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award – Canada, Alberta and NWT Division
duration: Self-paced across Bronze, Silver and Gold levels
location: Alberta-wide (completed in your own community through a school, cadet corps, Scouts group or independently)
eligibility: Youth aged 14 to 24. Bronze starts at 14, Silver at 15 and Gold at 16, and you may enter at any level once you meet its minimum age. Registration is through an Award Unit under the Alberta, NWT and Nunavut operating authority.
description: A non-competitive award earned by logging hours in four areas: physical recreation, a skill, voluntary service and an adventurous journey, with a residential project added at Gold. It is the standard way to get formal, internationally recognized credit for the sport, clubs and volunteering you are already doing, and it is recognized in more than 130 countries. Over 4,000 young Albertans are enrolled. Bronze is presented by a community leader, Silver by the Lieutenant Governor and Gold by the Governor General or a member of the Royal Family.

name: AAPT PhysicsBowl
grades: High school physics students (Division I first-year, Division II second-year)
duration: 45-minute exam, written on one day inside a two-week window in late March
location: School-based across Alberta (written at your own school, proctored); $10 per student
eligibility: Any high school physics student. The exam must be proctored by someone holding at least a two-year degree who is not related to a participant, and five students are needed to score as a school team.
description: Your teacher registers the school by late February; the exam is written between mid-March and early April. A 40-question multiple-choice physics contest run by the American Association of Physics Teachers, open to schools worldwide.

name: AMC 10 and AMC 12 (American Mathematics Competitions)
grades: AMC 12 for grade 12 and below, AMC 10 for grade 10 and below
duration: 75-minute exam, 25 questions, with an A date and a B date in November
location: School-based across Alberta (your school registers as a competition site); $55 early bird or $75 regular site fee, plus $30 per bundle of ten student licenses
eligibility: Students enrolled full time at a Canadian or American school. A competition manager at the school registers the site; students cannot enter on their own. High scorers are invited to the AIME.
description: The standard way to show quantitative rigour on an application to an American university, and the qualifying route to the AIME and the olympiad path beyond it. Twenty-five questions in 75 minutes on advanced algebra, geometry, number theory and combinatorics. For 2026/27 the A versions run November 5, 2026 and the B versions November 13, 2026. October 15, 2026 is the final registration deadline for a school that has never hosted before, so if no school near you offers it, ask a math teacher to sign up as a competition manager well ahead of that.

name: Rotary Adventure in Citizenship
provider: Rotary Club of Ottawa, with participants sponsored by local Rotary clubs
stipend: Travel and attendance covered by the sponsoring Rotary club
location: Ottawa (travel from Alberta paid by the nominating club)
eligibility: Canadian citizens or permanent residents aged 16 to 18 who are leaders in their community. Students are sponsored by a local Rotary club rather than applying centrally, so start with the Rotary club in your own town.
description: Apply through your local Rotary club — selection is run by clubs, not centrally, so ask yours about timing. Since 1951 the program has brought 150+ students aged 16-18 to Ottawa for four days of meetings with parliamentarians, plus access to three $1,000 scholarships.

name: Youth Parliament of Canada
stipend: Fully funded, covering travel, accommodation, meals and activities
location: Ottawa (fully funded from anywhere in Canada)
eligibility: 75 participants aged 16 to 20 chosen from every province and territory through a competitive application. The program runs bilingually.
description: A fully funded, bilingual parliamentary simulation on Parliament Hill run by CIVIX, the civic education charity behind Student Vote. Delegates take part in legislative debate, committee work and question period. The inaugural session ran November 6 to 10, 2025 with 75 delegates, the first youth parliament on the Hill in more than four decades. CIVIX had not announced a second session as of August 2026, so email youthparliament@civix.ca before counting on it. This is a new program and is unrelated to the 1980s parliament of the same name, which no longer runs.

name: League of Innovators
duration: Launch It is self-paced, Labs runs 12 weeks, Boost runs 12 months
stipend: Free and equity-free; Labs holds a $120 refundable deposit, Boost $250
location: Online, open to founders in every province
eligibility: Canadian founders aged 15 to 30 who are building something. Launch It is open enrolment. Labs and Boost are selective, judged on traction, fit and readiness for the stage.
description: The largest youth startup accelerator in Canada, a national charity founded by Hootsuite founder Ryan Holmes. Launch It is a free self-paced course for getting an idea off the ground. Labs is the flagship 12-week virtual accelerator, with workshops, mentors, AMA sessions and a cohort of other young founders. Boost is a 12-month program for founders further along. All three are free and take no equity, and the deposits are returned on completion. Applications for the fall 2026 Labs cohort opened in July 2026.

name: YETI – Young Entrepreneurs Training Initiative
provider: Community Futures Alberta (Capital Region, Big Country, Lakeland and Lac La Biche offices)
duration: Four days of training, then run the business across the eight weeks of summer
stipend: $500 in startup funding, plus up to $500 more for meeting milestones
location: Participating Community Futures regions in Alberta only, not province-wide (applications normally open in May)
eligibility: Senior high school students living in a participating Community Futures region. Check with your regional office first, since only four of the Alberta offices run the program.
description: Register through the Community Futures office in your area. YETI is a summer business-training program for senior high school students in the Capital Region — you launch a real business over the summer with startup funding and mentorship, and may earn high school credit.

name: Alberta Student Leadership Conference (ASLC)
provider: Alberta Association of Students' Councils and Advisors (AASCA)
grades: Junior and senior high students on student council or in a leadership class
duration: 3 days each May, Friday after school through Sunday noon
location: A different Alberta host school each year (2026: École Olds High School)
eligibility: Students attend as part of a school delegation with a staff advisor. Schools register the delegation; individual students cannot enter on their own.
description: The provincial student leadership conference, run since 1988 by a volunteer association of student council advisors and hosted by a different Alberta school every year. Three days of keynote speakers, around 14 breakout sessions, a service project and a dance, built around meeting student leaders from across the province. Useful for building a community leadership record rather than a competitive one. ASLC 2026 ran May 1 to 3 at École Olds High School; the 2027 host had not been announced as of August 2026. Ask your student council advisor to enter a delegation.

name: Rise for the World
provider: Rise, a program of Schmidt Futures and the Rhodes Trust
grades: Ages 15 to 17 as of July 1 of the cohort year
duration: Application project over several months, then lifetime membership if selected
stipend: Global Winners receive a four-year post-secondary scholarship, project funding and a technology package
location: Worldwide; the application is online and the summit is in person
eligibility: Open globally to young people aged 15 to 17 as of July 1 of the cohort year, with no citizenship restriction. You apply with a project or piece of work that serves other people, not with a transcript.
description: A global talent program that names 100 Global Winners a year and backs them for life. Winners get a four-year post-secondary scholarship covering tuition and a living stipend, awarded on need and only where other financial aid does not already cover it, plus a fully funded residential summit, a laptop or tablet, and the ability to apply for funding for their own projects later on. It suits students who already run something that serves other people rather than students with a strong report card alone. Check the status before you plan around it: the most recent cohort announced on the Rise site is 2024, and as of August 2026 the apply subdomain redirects to the homepage with no open cycle posted.

name: Non-Trivial Fellowship
duration: Online cohort program, part-time alongside school
stipend: Project grants at the Fellows tier and $10,000 scholarships at the Scholars tier
eligibility: Ages 14 to 20 who have not yet started university, anywhere in the world. Free to apply and free to take part. Selection is on curiosity and reasoning rather than grades.
description: An online research incubator where you pick a problem that matters, get matched with a mentor and produce a real piece of work over the cohort, in anything from policy and economics to computer science and biology. It runs in three tiers: Research Foundations gives a certificate and community access, Research Fellows adds mentorship and project grants, and Research Scholars adds custom mentorship and a $10,000 scholarship. Applications for the next cohort open in November 2026, with a priority deadline of December 15, 2026 and a final deadline of January 4, 2027. Widely circulated figures about a $500 acceptance award and $30,000 in seed funding are not on the Non-Trivial site as of August 2026, so treat the tiers above as the published offer.

name: Explore French Immersion Bursary
provider: Council of Ministers of Education, Canada, funded by the Government of Canada
grades: Ages 13 to 15 and 16 and up, depending on the host institution
duration: 31 to 33 days for ages 16 and up, spring or summer; 19 to 21 days for ages 13 to 15, summer only
stipend: Bursary covers tuition, instructional material, meals, accommodation and cultural activities
location: Host universities and colleges across Canada, including Quebec and the Atlantic provinces
eligibility: Canadian citizen or permanent resident who has been a student for at least one term in the current school year, or took part in Odyssey in the last two years. No French level is required, from beginner up. Places are awarded by a randomized computer draw, not on merit, and applicants who miss the first draw go into a wait pool for institutional draws from March to July.
description: Application portals open September 14, 2026 for the 2027 sessions. Explore is a federally funded bursary covering tuition, accommodation and meals for a spring or summer French immersion session in another province, for students aged 16 and up.

name: House of Commons Page Program
grades: Apply in Grade 12, work during your first year of university
duration: One academic year, about 15 hours a week around full-time studies
stipend: Around $18,400 for the year plus a $1,200 completion bonus, per the participating universities
location: Parliament Hill, Ottawa; you study at the University of Ottawa, Carleton, Saint Paul University or Université du Québec en Outaouais
eligibility: Canadian citizen or permanent resident graduating from high school, enrolling at an eligible institution in the National Capital Region in September, willing to live in the region, and fluent in both official languages. Bilingualism is formally assessed, so plan your French ahead of the application.
description: Forty students are chosen from across Canada each year to work on the floor of the House of Commons while doing their first year of university in Ottawa. Pages carry documents and messages during sittings, work directly around Members of Parliament and see federal legislation as it happens, which is experience almost nothing else at that age can match. Recruitment runs on a long cycle: applications for the 2027 to 2028 cohort open in September 2026 and close in November 2026, selections finish in March 2027 and offers go out at the end of April 2027. You apply in your Grade 12 year, so the timing lines up with university applications.

name: City of Edmonton Youth Council
grades: High school and post-secondary age youth in Edmonton
duration: Appointed term of roughly one to two years, with monthly meetings plus committee work
location: Edmonton (meetings at City Hall, first Wednesday of the month, 5:30 to 8:30 pm)
eligibility: Edmonton youth appointed by City Council through an annual recruitment normally held in May. The age range and residency terms are set in each year's posting, so email youthcouncil@edmonton.ca for the current criteria.
description: An official civic agency, not a simulation. Members research and write policy proposals that go to City Council, run events on local youth issues and advise on decisions that affect young Edmontonians, which makes it verifiable government experience rather than a mock exercise. Meetings are open to the public if you want to sit in before applying. Other Alberta municipalities run comparable youth councils or advisory committees, so if you are outside Edmonton, check your own city or town's civic agency listings for the local equivalent.

name: Vimy Pilgrimage Award
duration: About one week in April, plus preparation before departure
stipend: Fully funded, including travel, accommodation and all program costs
eligibility: Canadian youth aged 15 to 17 with a demonstrated record of service to their community. Competitive written application; no cost to recipients.
description: A fully funded week in Belgium and France studying Canada's role in the First World War on the ground, visiting battlefields, cemeteries and museums with a national cohort of students. It rewards community service and historical interest rather than marks, and it carries real weight on a scholarship application later. The 2026 journey ran April 3 to 11 and its application window was October 21 to November 25, 2025. The next cycle had not been posted as of August 2026, so watch the page from mid-October.
